what: Reviewer-model trial 1: the same 27 harvested W3 review rounds as replay-1, with the reviewer (and its verdict turn) on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B nothink instead of qwen3.8-nothink. Same round-2 packets, prompts, REVIEW_STEPS 20 and verdict turn. The candidate was served by worker llmbench01 (ik llama-server, config C2, locked to the sandbox) through `replay-reviews --reviewer-model w1/qwen3.6 --worker ...`: no router or chat-server change, no window, the user's chat untouched.

candidate.served_by: llmbench01 (172.16.10.205:8090), ik llama-server C2: -c 65536 -t 12 -tb 16 -ub 1024 -b 2048 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -rtr -cram 256 -ctx-ckpt 8, temp 0.7 top-p 0.8 top-k 20
candidate.hardware: one Minisforum BD795i SE (CPU only); the GPU reviewer in replay-1 ran on the V620 pair

result.one_step_verdicts: 12 of 27 (decided from the packet alone, no tool call)
result.tool_errors: a few `glob` calls timed out (ripgrep over the tree); no model or API errors

disagreements_with_qwen3.8_read_by_hand.read: GAIN: the only reviewer to refuse a state that fails the hidden tests (the lane re-check releases one slot, not both).
GAIN: catches the should_cache arity bug (TypeError on every HTTP-200 search) that qwen3.8 accepted in 3 steps; W3 agrees.
MISS: the redirect urljoin bug qwen3.8 found is real; qwen3.6 did not see it.
MISS (soft): both other reviewers asked for real fixes to the shipped zfs-import unit (wrong comment, live-host behaviour); the tests do not cover them.
SPURIOUS: claims `except (*_REQUEST_EXCEPTIONS, RuntimeError):` raises TypeError; that is valid Python (PEP 448). A hallucinated bug, one rework round of cost.
SPURIOUS: the 'logical bug' it describes is the lock doing its job (the second caller sees the first caller's row). Hallucinated, one rework round of cost.

assessment.quality: about the same as qwen3.8 on these 27 rounds: it caught two things qwen3.8 missed (one of them a state the hidden tests fail) and missed two things qwen3.8 caught; the new failure mode is the hallucinated bug in a 1-step verdict (2 of 27), which costs a rework round each.
assessment.cost: 3x fewer reviewer steps (median 3 vs 10) and 40% less wall time per review even on a CPU box; on the V620s a 3B-active MoE would be several times faster still than the 27B dense reviewer.
assessment.verdicts: always a verdict; 1 capped round rescued by the verdict turn, like qwen3.8.
assessment.recommendation: a credible reviewer for the throughput question, not a quality upgrade. If the lead stays the bottleneck after the round-2 window, measure it on the GPU as an extra arm (T with the qwen3.6 reviewer) in a later window rather than changing the pre-registered one; keep qwen3.8 as the fixer. Mitigation worth trying first: require at least one tool call (a read of the changed function) before a verdict, to cut the 1-step hallucinations.

teardown: worker torn down (key shredded, lock removed), wf-replay2 router key revoked, host keys shredded, VM key files 0, no key in the harvest; harvest at /root/wf/runs/replay-2 on the host
